paragraphs: Art. 1. Entry consists in giving publicity to the acts subject to entry in the manner provided in these Regulations.
Art. 2. An entry, a note and a deletion are allowed only in the cases expressly provided for in the laws.
Art. 3. (1) Only acts made by notarial procedure or with a notarially certified signature are subject to entry.
(2) This does not apply to acts issued by the competent state bodies.

4.title: Acts entered
paragraphs: Art. 4. The following are entered:

a) all acts that transfer ownership (sale, gift, exchange, giving in payment, transfer against maintenance and care, etc.) or create, transfer, change or end another real right (right of use, ownership of a building, etc.) in real estate, and acts recognising such rights (declaratory notarial deeds, acts with the force of declaratory deeds, acts of state and municipal property and others expressly provided by law);
b) contracts transferring an inheritance (Art. 212 of the Obligations and Contracts Act);
c) acts waiving real rights in real estate (Art. 100 of the Property Act);
d) contracts for partition of real estate and court partition protocols;
e) requests of the deceased's creditors or legatees for separation of the deceased's real estate (Art. 67 of the Inheritance Act);
f) leases of real estate, including agricultural land, for more than one year (Art. 237 of the Obligations and Contracts Act);
g) settlements of disputes about acts subject to entry; and
h) final court decisions that replace the acts under letter "a", and decisions establishing the existence of acts subject to entry under the preceding letters;
i) acts correcting an obvious factual error in entered acts;

j) copies of announced wills concerning real estate and rights in real estate; for a universal will, the presence of real estate in the judicial district is certified by a declaration with a notarially certified signature of the beneficiary, listing the known properties in that district, presented with the will to the registration judge of the district where the property is;
k) all other acts that the law makes subject to entry.

6.title: Content of acts for entry
paragraphs: Art. 6. (1) Acts subject to entry must contain:

a) the first, father's and family name, the residence (permanent address) and the personal number of the parties, or in the cases of the BULSTAT Act the foreigner's number or BULSTAT code, and without one the place and date of birth; for a merchant or legal entity, the firm and legal form, the registration court, case number, seat and BULSTAT code, and for those in the Commercial Register the UIC; for entities without court registration in Bulgaria, the firm, seat and BULSTAT code;
b) the date and place of issue of the act;
c) the description of the property, with its type, location (municipality, settlement, address, locality), number, area and/or built-up area, and boundaries;
d) the price of the property or the right, or the certified material interest.
(2) No description of the property is required for:
a) copies of announced wills, whether or not a property is stated and whether the beneficiary knows of properties in the district;
b) acts concerning a whole of which real estate may be part, contracts transferring an inheritance, acts transforming companies, pledge contracts and contracts transferring a commercial enterprise.

(3) When the property is in an area with an approved cadastral map, the description follows the data under Art. 60, items 1–7 of the Cadastre and Property Register Act. A sketch, draft sketch, scheme or draft scheme issued by the Cadastre Agency, or notarially certified copies of them, are attached to the act.
(4) Para. 3 does not apply to entries, notes and deletions under Art. 11, 17, 18, 19, 22, 22a(1) and (3), 23, 24, 25, 26 and 31.

Art. 7. The entry is made on the order of the registration judge of the registry office where the real estate is, by filing the acts subject to entry in books that are open to the public under section VII and that consist of:
a) the notarial deeds under Art. 4, letter "a", filed in order, and
b) all other acts under Art. 4, filed in order.

Art. 8. (1) The notarial deeds under Art. 4, letter "a" are entered on the written request of the notary who made them; all other acts under Art. 4, or copies of them, on the written request of the parties, of a notary or of anybody with an interest in the entry. Notarial deeds made by the registration judge and copies of wills announced by the judge are entered of the judge's own motion.

(2) For the entry of the notarial deeds under Art. 4, letter "a", two identical originals are presented. For the entry of all other acts under Art. 4, the original and an officially certified copy of it are presented, or two such copies if the original cannot be presented; for announced wills concerning real estate and rights in real estate, two notarially certified copies. When the entry is made on the request of a notary, three identical copies, or three copies, are presented.
(3) An entry of officially certified extracts is also allowed; they must contain the essential terms of the act entered.

9.title: Procedure of entry
paragraphs: Art. 9. (1) The entry is made on the order of the registration judge immediately after the act is recorded in the incoming register; the act itself shows the register number, the date and the volume and page of the file book. Where software for auxiliary property files is used, the number of the auxiliary file is also written on the act.
(2) The act is filed in the respective book, and within 3 days the second copy of the entered act is returned to the applicant.
(3) When the entry is made on a notary's request, the third and following copies are returned, each with the data under para. 1.

(4) An act made by the registration judge is entered immediately after it is made. The registration judge may not, on pain of liability, order any other action between making such an act and its entry.

11.title: Entry of claims
paragraphs: Art. 11. The following must be entered or noted:

a) claims for termination (Art. 87(3) of the Obligations and Contracts Act), annulment (Art. 32), revocation (Art. 227 of that Act and Art. 37 of the Inheritance Act) or declaration of nullity (Art. 26) of acts subject to entry under Art. 4;
b) claims for a decision on the conclusion of a final contract (Art. 19(3) of the Obligations and Contracts Act) that transfers or creates a real right in real estate; and
c) claims for other decisions under Art. 4, letters "h", "j" and "k".

Art. 12. (1) For the entry or the note under Art. 11, the statement of claim filed with the court, on which the state fee for opening the case was paid, is presented together with a copy or an extract of it. The statement of claim must meet the requirements of Art. 6.

(2) The entry is made on the order of the registration judge by writing briefly the relief sought in the claim in the personal partida concerned. The copy of the claim is filed in a special office file, and the original is returned to the court where the case was opened. If the claim concerns several acts, the record in the partida book is made against the record of each of them.
(3) If the act to which the claim refers is not entered, the claim is entered under the procedure of Art. 9.
Art. 13. The entry under the preceding article is deleted by noting in the partida book the court act that orders the deletion or that terminates the proceedings in the case.

Art. 14. The final decisions on the claims under Art. 11 are noted in the manner set out in Art. 12, on a copy of the decision presented. In that case the decision must also meet the requirements of Art. 6.

Art. 19. (1) The entry of a mortgage (Art. 179 of the Obligations and Contracts Act) is deleted on the written consent of the creditor, given in notarially certified form, or on a final court act that orders the deletion. When the creditor is a state body, no certification of the signature is required.

(2) A mortgage on real estate sold at a public sale is deleted on the request of the buyer. With the request, the buyer presents the final order of award of the property, entered in the books of entries, and a certificate of the bailiff that the buyer did not take over the mortgage by agreement with the mortgage creditor under Art. 175(2) of the Obligations and Contracts Act.

(3) Anybody with an interest may request the deletion. It is made by a note on the side of the entered act that states the document on which it is based and the time when it is made. The note is signed by the registration judge. When there is no free space left on the mortgage deed, an official of the registry office, on the order of the registration judge, attaches an extension sheet fixed with the official's signature and the seal of the office in at least two places. The registration judge makes a special remark about the extension after the certification under Art. 35(3).
Art. 22. When 10 years have passed from the date of the entry and it was not renewed, the deletion is made on the request of the person concerned, without other evidence.

Art. 32a. (1) When the act recorded in the incoming register does not meet the requirements of the law or is not subject to entry, the registration judge rules a refusal. The act is recorded in the register of refusals under Art. 33, letter "n", with the refusal and its date.

(2) The acts for which a refusal was ruled are filed in the book of refusals under Art. 33, letter "o". Every two hundred filed copies form one volume. Each volume starts a new numbering of its sheets. The numbering of the acts and the volumes starts again each year.
(3) (Repealed.)

(4) The ruling of refusal is served on the person concerned against signature. The appeal against the refusal and the final ruling of the regional court are recorded in the register of refusals under Art. 33, letter "n", at the number of the refusal itself, and are filed in the book under Art. 33, letter "o".
(5) (Repealed.)
Art. 32b. The rules of Art. 32a also apply accordingly to a refusal of a note and a refusal of a deletion.

Art. 32c. When the appeal against a refusal of an entry, a note or a deletion is granted, the entry, the note or the deletion is deemed made from the moment the act was recorded in the incoming register.
Art. 33c. (1) A technical error is any mismatch between the content of the entered act and the data from it recorded in the respective partidas.

(2) Technical errors are established on the request of the person concerned or of a notary, or of the office's own motion by an official of the registry office. For the error found, the official draws up a declaratory protocol, signs it and presents it to the head of the Registry Agency or to a person designated by the head.
(3) A technical error is corrected on the order of the head of the Registry Agency or of a person designated by the head.
Art. 46. (1) A certificate for a person shows only the entries, notes and deletions made in the name of one person or of several named persons.
(2) The application for the certificate under para. 1 must contain the data under Art. 6(1), letter "a".
Art. 47. (1) A certificate issued for a particular property lists the entries, notes and deletions of encumbrances and rights, or certifies that there are none.
(2) The application for the certificate under para. 1 must show:
a) the data under Art. 46(2) of the persons to whom the inquiry relates and of their direct predecessors in title;
b) the real estate, with the data under Art. 6(1), letter "c".
(3) (Repealed.)
